Start with what a simulation must let you do—not with available layouts or
solver commands. The **Pages × Notebook suite** connects candidate requirements
to canonical notebook cases. Pages explain the intended product and observations;
notebooks own concrete settings and real tool calls. No new solved results are
claimed for the source-only suite.

OrPen owns fabrication facts, public source layouts and the user's model intent.
SCGSim owns the reusable toolchain that must carry those facts through native
modeling, execution and returned results. A notebook is an operation and
evidence entry point; it does not replace either contract.

## Two requirement perspectives

The layers describe **who needs what**, not a ranking of important and minor
features.

- **Layer 1 · OrPen user requirements** states the physical product and the
  high-level Palace/AEDT workflow required to produce it.
- **Layer 2 · SCGSim tool requirements** states the geometry, model, numerical
  evidence and portable-result requirements shared by those workflows.

OrPen is the requirements customer: it supplies source/process facts and model
intent, and inspects the final product. SCGSim owns implementation and solver
integration. These pages do not prescribe API calls or track implementation status.

Read a Layer 1 page first, follow its Layer 2 links, and only then select a
layout and notebook. One requirement may need several notebooks; one layout
may support several requirements. Neither count is fixed.

## Layer 1 · OrPen user requirements

| I need to… | Requirement contract |
| --- | --- |
| Extract capacitance with an explicit conductor/reference convention | [Electrostatic and capacitance extraction](simulation/requirements/electrostatic-capacitance.qmd) |
| Find modes of an explicitly bounded electromagnetic model | [Ordinary eigenmode](simulation/requirements/eigenmode.qmd) |
| Include explicit linear circuit loads in a mode calculation | [Lumped RLC eigenmode](simulation/requirements/lumped-rlc-eigenmode.qmd) |
| Interpret participation and loss with declared field and interface provenance | [EPR and loss analysis](simulation/requirements/epr-loss.qmd) |
| Excite a terminal network through Lumped or Wave ports | [Driven Terminal](simulation/requirements/driven-terminal.qmd) |
| Excite and read a modal port network | [Driven Modal](simulation/requirements/driven-modal.qmd) |
| Extract resistance and inductance with real source/sink assignments | [Q3D AC/RL extraction](simulation/requirements/q3d-acrl.qmd) |
| Extract per-unit-length quantities from an authored cross-section | [Q2D cross-section extraction](simulation/requirements/q2d-cross-section.qmd) |

## Layer 2 · SCGSim tool requirements

Use [source and ownership](simulation/tools/source-ownership.qmd) to bind
identities; [curves, holes and transforms](simulation/tools/curves-holes-transforms.qmd)
to preserve shape meaning; [materials, stack and Z](simulation/tools/materials-stack-z.qmd)
to declare physical representation; and [contacts and multilevel structures](simulation/tools/contacts-multilevel.qmd)
to distinguish contact from overlap. [Mesh, FEM and AMR](simulation/tools/mesh-fem-amr.qmd)
covers discretization evidence. [Handoff, Resolve and Report](simulation/tools/handoff-resolve-report.qmd)
covers the usable returned workflow.

## Select evidence, not just a picture

A [source inspection plate](public-pdk-examples/test-components.md) shows the
authored geometry. It is not evidence of native lowering, conductor assignment,
mesh conformity or solving. Track source availability, preparation, native
model readback, solving, strict resolution and reporting separately.

The [notebook catalog](simulation/notebooks.qmd) links source ownership,
curves/holes/transforms and multilevel contact observations; pad and finite-CPW
cases; shared RLC and Lumped/Wave Terminal cases; and Q2D extraction. It also
keeps historical examples and evidence separate. A linked notebook is a candidate
starting point, not proof that it satisfies a new requirement. Missing source
semantics or unsupported operations stay visible; do not fill them with guessed
native identities or plausible output.

## Review and next steps

Review physical meaning and expected observations before choosing concrete
operation controls. These contracts introduce no numerical accuracy threshold
or solver-agreement criterion. Native convergence classifications and warnings
remain visible, but do not themselves establish research adequacy.

The current suite remains **CONVERGING / LOCAL CANDIDATE**. Its clean derived
notebooks are source-only, with native preparation, meshing and solving
separately controlled. The ordinary environment and dependency pins remain
unchanged. Historical output is not execution of a revised source.
